narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the lack of any property you could offer as security, and the length of the loan you requested. 

Your checking account balance sits in the 0-200 DM range, a situation shared by only 18% of approved applicants and far less favorable than the 59% who hold no checking account at all. This single detail pushed the prediction most strongly toward rejection. The fact that you have no property to pledge added further weight in the same negative direction; most successful applicants own either real estate or a vehicle that can serve as collateral. Finally, the 36-month repayment period you asked for is almost twice as long as the 19-month average among those who were approved, which also increased the assessed risk.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed several positive aspects of your profile, such as your steady job in management and your clean credit history of bills paid on time.

To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on building a larger and more visible checking-account balance, acquiring some form of tangible asset, and, if possible, shortening the loan term you request. Addressing these areas will directly tackle the reasons the model turned you down today. (248 words)
